title: NABA Meet & Greet Event In Glasgow  - Parkhead School House  2:00pm to 5:00pm
description: National African & Black Association (NABA) is delighted to invite you to our Meet & Greet Official Event on Friday, 18 September 2026, from 2:00pm to 5:00pm at Parkhead SchoolHouse, 135 Westmuir Street, Glasgow, G31 5EX . This special gathering is an opportunity to bring together members of the African and Black community, local organisations, professionals, community leaders, partners and friends to connect, build meaningful relationships and discover what NABA has to offer. Come along to learn more about our vision and work, share ideas, explore opportunities for partnership and collaboration , and discover how we can work together to empower our community, strengthen networks and create positive change. Whether you are already involved in community activities or simply interested in making a difference, your presence is warmly welcomed. Let’s connect, let’s collaborate, and let’s make a difference because we are stronger together and better together. For more information, visit www.nabaorg.uk , email admin@nabaorg.uk , or call/text +447990753498 to confirm your attendance.

title: NABA in partnership with West Lothian Race Forum Black History Month Seminar 2026
description: "DOES ETHNIC MINORITIES IN SCOTLAND HAVE A SAY?" Seminar Purpose The seminar will bring together representatives from ethnic minority communities, government, local authorities, public services, business, education, health, justice, sport, the third sector and political life to examine whether ethnic minority people in Scotland have meaningful opportunities to influence the decisions that affect their lives. The discussion should move beyond consultation towards the question of; power, representation, accountability and measurable change . Our approach reflects Scotland's current policy direction, which seeks greater use of lived experience and public participation in shaping policy and decision-making.

title: National African & Black Association (NABA) 2 Days Strategic Workshop Report
description: A two-day strategic workshop held by the National African & Black Association (NABA) in 2024. The workshop aimed to create awareness of NABA and collectively set a strategic pathway for the organisation. Introduction NABA was formed as a legacy of the Sheku Bayoh Campaign for equity and fairer justice in Scotland. It is a non-profit organisation focused on promoting access to education, employment, healthcare, and justice for African and Black communities in Scotland and the UK. NABA addresses systemic issues such as racism, stereotyping, and limited accessibility to services. Objectives and Mission NABA's objectives include promoting anti-racism, supporting victim families, promoting equity, fighting injustice, preventing poverty, creating opportunities, engaging in cultural and community activities, and advocating for the rights of African and Black communities. Organisational Structure NABA is governed by a hierarchical structure, including key members such as the Directors, Chief Executive Officer, Executive Ambassadors, Executive Members, Employees, Internship, volunteers and Community group representatives. The organisation also encourages participation from community ambassadors and volunteers. Workshop Aim and Outcome The aim of the workshop was to increase awareness of NABA and set a strategic pathway. The outcomes included identifying key issues such as poverty prevention, racism, hate crimes, immigration, workplace discrimination, mental health & public health, issues with social work services, education , safety, hard to reach organisations and more. The workshop provided a platform to share experiences and knowledge on tackling these issues. Day 1: Strategic Planning The first day focused on outlining the organisation's areas of interest, identifying community stakeholders, drafting MOUs, and formulating strategic outcomes for the year. Day 2: Policing Together and Strategic Development The second day involved collaboration with Police Scotland, discussing strategic outcomes, and developing a methodology for Community safety and feeling safe MOUs and service level agreements. Annual Activities and Events The document also lists various annual activities and events planned by NABA, including the Day of African Child, African Market, Fund Raising Dinner, Wealth Building Conference, promoting & participation in community events and more."
